seo_title: Free XDR brightness boost for Mac
seo_description: XdrBoostBar is a free, open-source menu bar app that unlocks the extra HDR headroom of MacBook Pro and XDR displays with one slider. Native, offline, macOS 14+.
hero_sub: XdrBoostBar uses the extra HDR headroom of your MacBook Pro or XDR display to make everyday content brighter. Drag the slider, or press Control + Option + B to toggle it.
features_sub: A small menu bar app that adds brightness on top of the system level and backs off when your Mac needs it to.

features.title: Boost slider from 0 to 100%
features.desc: Sets how much extra brightness is added on top of the system level. The multiplier is capped at 2x and never exceeds what the display reports as available.

features.title: Global hotkey toggle
features.desc: Press Control + Option + B from any app to switch the boost on or off. The sun icon in the menu bar shows whether it is on, off or unsupported.

features.title: Per-display detection
features.desc: Displays with EDR headroom are detected automatically and listed with their headroom. You choose which ones get the boost, and unsupported setups are clearly labeled.

features.title: Battery saver
features.desc: Pauses the boost on battery below a threshold you set, 30% by default, and whenever Low Power Mode is on.

features.title: Thermal protection
features.desc: If the system reaches a serious or critical thermal state, the boost ramps down over about a second and the popover shows a notice.

features.title: Compatibility mode
features.desc: If the default overlay method does not brighten your screen, switch to a gamma-table method. Gamma settings are restored when the boost turns off and when the app quits.

faq.q: Is XdrBoostBar really free and open source?
faq.a: Yes. It is released under the MIT license and the full source is on GitHub. There are no ads, analytics or paid tiers, and an optional Ko-fi donation button is the only way to support it.
None. The hotkey does not need Accessibility access, and the app draws its own overlay without capturing the screen, so Screen Recording is not needed either. It makes no network connections.
Only on your Mac. Your settings are saved locally in the app's standard macOS preferences so they persist between launches. Nothing is sent anywhere.

faq.q: Why is the app not notarized?
faq.a: Notarization requires a paid Apple Developer account, and this is a free project. Right-click the app and choose Open once to get past Gatekeeper, or build it yourself from source with Xcode.
